diagnostics.title: Duplicate element id
diagnostics.summary: Two elements in one template always render with the same literal id. An id must be unique in the page, so a label's for attribute, aria-labelledby, URL fragments, and getElementById find only the first element.
diagnostics.when: Two elements have the same static id value, and neither is inside a condition or a loop: c-if, c-elif, c-else, c-for, or c-empty, as a tag or as an attribute on the element or around it; v-if, v-else-if, v-else, or v-for; a c-fill, a <c-slot> fallback, the body of a component tag, or a <template>. Those may render an element zero or several times, so the check cannot know whether both appear. v-show does not count, because a hidden element is still in the page. The same id coming from two templates is not reported. citry check --static and an editor that has not loaded your application report it too, with the severity the component's own Lint class sets as a plain string.
diagnostics.fix: Give one of the elements another id.

messages.default: Another element in this template already has id '{id}'. An id must be unique in the page.

diagnostics.title: Image without alt text
diagnostics.summary: An has no alt text. A screen reader then reads out the file name or nothing useful, and the image has no text when it fails to load.
diagnostics.when: An has no alt in any form (alt, c-alt, :alt, or v-bind:alt), no aria-label or aria-labelledby, and no role="none" or role="presentation". An image with a c-bind or v-bind spread is not reported, because the spread may add alt. Neither is an that is a component's only top-level element, or the only element in each block of a top-level c-if, c-elif, and c-else chain, when the component may have browser code (JavaScript, js_data(), State, or event handlers), because Vue passes the alt that a parent writes on the component's tag to that element. A component whose JavaScript sets inheritAttrs: false in $component({...}) stops Vue from passing it, so that image is reported. citry check without --static, and an editor that has loaded your application, report that image when the component has no browser code or sets inheritAttrs: false. citry check --static and an editor that has not loaded your application report the other images too, but never a component's only top-level , with the severity the component's own Lint class sets as a plain string.
diagnostics.fix: Describe the image in alt. For an image that only decorates the page, write alt="" so screen readers skip it.

messages.default: has no alt text. Describe the image in alt, or write alt="" for an image that only decorates the page.

diagnostics.title: Link to a missing page or file
diagnostics.summary: A link, image, script, or form points at a path on your site that none of your app's routes or static files serves, so the browser gets a 404 Not Found.
diagnostics.when: An HTML element's href, src, or action is a path that starts with a single /, such as /about or /static/logo.svg, and your web framework answers that it serves no such path. Citry asks the framework that mounts it: Flask's URL rules and static folders when you call citry.contrib.flask.mount(), the routes and StaticFiles mounts of a FastAPI or Starlette app when you call citry.contrib.fastapi.mount(), and Django's URL patterns and static file finders when you call citry.contrib.django.urlpatterns(). The query string and fragment are ignored. These are not checked: a URL with a scheme, such as https: or mailto:; a //host/... URL; a relative path; a value written as an expression, such as :href or c-href; a <base href> or a <link rel="preconnect"> or rel="dns-prefetch"; a path under the prefix Citry's own routes are mounted at; a parameter type that only the view checks, such as a FastAPI project_id: int argument; and, with Django, a path under MEDIA_URL. The rule runs in citry check with your application loaded, and in an editor that has loaded your application, and only when one of those calls runs while Citry imports the module that --app, or the editor's citry.app setting, names. The editor checks the paths your templates hold when it loads your application, so a path you add later is checked after the next load. A path that another server answers for your site, such as a reverse proxy, is reported too, which is why the rule is a warning.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the path, or add the route or file. If another server answers the path, set rule_unknown_url to "ignore" in the component's Lint class, or for the whole app in LintSettings.

parameters.path: The path the browser requests, without its query string and fragment.
parameters.suggestion: A path your app serves that is one typing slip from it.

messages.default: Your app has no route or static file for '{path}', so the browser gets a 404 Not Found.
messages.suggestion: Your app has no route or static file for '{path}', so the browser gets a 404 Not Found. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?

diagnostics.title: Shared value read under a key nothing provides
diagnostics.summary: A component reads a shared value with self.inject("key"), but no component above it provides that key, so rendering it raises KeyError.
diagnostics.when: A method of a component class, or of a base class or mixin it extends, calls self.inject() with one string literal and no default, and no provider Citry can see gives that key to the component. Citry starts at each template that uses the component's tag, such as <c-card />, and walks up through the templates that use those components. A key counts when a <c-provide key="..."> wraps the tag; when a component on the way calls self.provide() with it; when the tag is slot content and the component whose <c-slot> shows it wraps that <c-slot> in <c-provide> or calls self.provide(); when a <c-component c-is="...">, which may render any component, sits inside a <c-provide> with the key or in a component that calls self.provide() with it; or when a render(provides={...}) call in your project's Python files passes it as a literal key, which counts for every component. A key written as a module-level string constant, also one imported from another module of the project, counts as that string. If the component appears in several places and one of them provides the key, nothing is reported. When no template uses the component's tag, because Python renders it or a <c-component c-is="..."> picks it, or when it is used only inside a group of templates that use each other and that no template outside the group uses, the key is compared with every key the app provides anywhere. Citry reports nothing for a call with a default, such as self.inject("key", None), a key written as a name or expression, or a call in a class from an installed package; below a <c-provide c-key="...">, a self.provide() key written as an expression, a tag inside a <c-component c-is="...">, markup in a component's attribute, or a component Python builds inside a component's methods or passes to another component, such as Layout(slots={"default": Widget()}); below a component whose Python source it cannot read and whose code calls provide(); and nothing at all while a registered template cannot be parsed or when the folder citry check runs from holds more than 20,000 Python files. A key the page does provide is reported when Citry cannot see the provider: a provides dictionary built elsewhere, a self.provide() call in a helper function, a template string rendered from Python, or a render(provides=...) call outside the folder you run citry check from. That is why the rule is a warning. The rule runs in citry check with your application loaded, and in an editor that has loaded your application; the editor checks the calls in the file you edit against the keys your app provided when it last loaded.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the key to the one the page provides, or provide the key above the component. Pass a default, such as self.inject("key", None), when the value is optional. If the key comes from somewhere Citry cannot see, set rule_unknown_inject_key to "ignore" in the component's Lint class, or for the whole app in LintSettings.

parameters.component: The name of the component class that calls inject().
parameters.suggestion: A provided key that is one typing slip from it.

messages.default: No component above {component} provides '{key}', so self.inject('{key}') raises KeyError when the page renders. Provide '{key}' above {component}, or pass a default to inject().
messages.suggestion: No component above {component} provides '{key}', so self.inject('{key}') raises KeyError when the page renders. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?
messages.nowhere: Nothing in your app provides '{key}', so self.inject('{key}') in {component} raises KeyError when the page renders. Provide '{key}' above {component}, or pass a default to inject().
messages.nowhereSuggestion: Nothing in your app provides '{key}', so self.inject('{key}') in {component} raises KeyError when the page renders. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?

diagnostics.title: JsData field is not a JSON type
diagnostics.summary: A JsData field has a type that cannot be sent to the browser as JSON, such as a set or a date. Editor help treats the value as any. A citry.Secret is reported too, because rendering refuses to send one.
diagnostics.when: A declared or inferred JsData field has a type that strict JSON cannot carry, such as bytes, a set, a callable, a date or time, or a whole class instance. A citry.Secret counts too: Citry never sends one to the browser, and rendering the component raises TypeError. With your application loaded, citry check also reads a module-level value that js_data() puts in its result, such as {"token": API_TOKEN} for API_TOKEN = Secret(...), and reports it when its value is not JSON. It reads such a value when it is the whole result, a value or item of a dict, list, or tuple literal in it, a name unpacked into a list such as [*TOKENS], either branch of a conditional expression, or the argument of Const(...); the value may be an attribute of a module-level name, such as config.API_TOKEN where config is a module or a plain class, when reading it runs no code: a property, or an object with a __getattr__ hook such as Django's lazy settings, is not read. A value read through an attribute is judged only when it is built from plain dicts, lists, tuples, strings, numbers, booleans, None, and Secrets. A module-level value holding another kind of object is reported only when that object's class could never pass the JSON check, so a lazy object or a dict subclass is skipped. A value nested too deeply to read is skipped. Without --types, a value that a call computes, such as get_token(), is not read. The editor and citry check --types also report a value that ty, the Python type checker Citry runs, types as a standard library type JSON cannot carry, such as PurePosixPath, datetime, Decimal, UUID, a set, or complex, or as a Secret.
diagnostics.fix: Convert the value to JSON-friendly data in js_data(), such as a list, a string, or a dict of plain values, and change the JsData annotation to match. For a Secret, read its value on the server with get_secret_value() where you need it, and leave it out of js_data().

parameters.name: JsData field name.
parameters.detail: Why the value is not a clean JSON type.

messages.default: JsData field '{name}' is not a clean JSON value: {detail}. Browser tooling will treat its type as unknown.
messages.secret: JsData field '{name}' can hold a citry.Secret, and rendering this component raises TypeError when it does: {detail}.

examples.title: Unsupported set value

diagnostics.title: JsData field conflicts with a public instance name
diagnostics.summary: A JsData field has the same name as something already on the component instance in the browser, such as a prop, a method, or a name Vue reserves.
diagnostics.when: A JsData field that Citry can see in the source uses a reserved browser name or the name of a Vue Options entry, such as a prop, method, or computed value.
diagnostics.fix: Rename the JsData field, or rename the Vue Options entry it collides with.

messages.default: JsData field '{name}' conflicts with a reserved or component-defined public instance name.
messages.conditional: JsData field '{name}' conflicts with a reserved or component-defined public instance name when supplied.

diagnostics.title: Misspelled css_data() variable
diagnostics.summary: A component's CSS reads a custom property that is one typing slip from a key its css_data() returns, such as var(--acent) for accent. Nothing sets that property, so the CSS property that reads it gets its inherited or initial value.
diagnostics.when: A var(--name) in the component's own css or css_file has no fallback value, the same CSS does not set --name itself, every key that css_data() or CssData returns is known, name is not one of them, and name is one typing slip from one of them: two neighboring letters swapped, one letter typed twice, or one letter left out. Properties that a parent component or a site stylesheet sets are not reported unless they are that close to a key. citry check needs your application for this rule.
diagnostics.fix: Use the key's exact name. If another stylesheet sets this property on purpose, add a fallback, as in var(--name, inherit), or set rule_misspelled_css_variable to "ignore" for this component.

parameters.name: The custom property as written, without the leading --.
parameters.suggestion: The css_data() key one typing slip away.

messages.default: Nothing sets --{name}, so this property gets its initial or inherited value. Did you mean --{suggestion}, from css_data()?

diagnostics.title: Misspelled CSS class
diagnostics.summary: A class in a template is one typing slip from a class the component's own CSS styles, such as bord for board. No CSS that Citry reads styles the class as written, so the element renders without those styles.
diagnostics.when: A static class attribute in a component's template, on an HTML element or a component tag, holds a class of three or more characters that is one typing slip from a class selector in the component's own css or css_file: two neighboring letters swapped, one letter typed twice, or one letter left out. These slips usually name another class of the same family, so they do not count: one that moves, doubles, or drops a digit, such as col-1 for col-12; a missing final s after a letter other than s, such as tab for tabs; one of these short words, as the whole class or as its last word after a hyphen or underscore, next to its longer form: close (closed), collapse (collapsed), disable (disabled), enable (enabled), fade (faded), mute (muted), show (shown), slide (slider), and toggle (toggled or toggler), such as navbar-toggle for navbar-toggler; and one letter typed twice or left out in a first hyphen-separated part of one or two characters, such as p-4 for px-4 or m-auto for ml-auto. Two letters swapped in that part, such as iu-button for ui-button, are reported. The class is reported only when no CSS that Citry reads declares it: no selector in a registered component's css, css_file, inline or local-file Dependencies stylesheet, or template <style> element that holds CSS names it, and no attribute selector such as [class^="btn-"] matches it. Bound classes, such as :class, v-bind:class, and c-class, words inside {{ }} in a class attribute, and classes on tags that render no element, such as c-if or template, are not checked. citry check needs your application for this rule; the editor does not run it.
diagnostics.fix: Use the class name the CSS styles. If a stylesheet that Citry does not read styles this class on purpose, set rule_misspelled_css_class to "ignore" for this component.

parameters.name: The class as written.
parameters.suggestion: The class from the component's CSS one typing slip away.

messages.default: No CSS that Citry reads styles the class '{name}'. Did you mean '{suggestion}', from this component's CSS?

examples.title: A dropped letter

diagnostics.title: Class that no CSS declares
diagnostics.summary: A class in a template is not named by any CSS that Citry reads, so either nothing styles it or a stylesheet outside Citry does.
diagnostics.when: The rule is off by default, because it also reports classes from a site stylesheet or a CSS framework such as Tailwind, and classes used only by JavaScript or tests. With rule_undeclared_css_class set to "warning" or "error", it reports each class in a static class attribute, on an HTML element or a component tag, that no CSS Citry reads declares. A class counts as declared when a selector in a registered component's css, css_file, inline or local-file Dependencies stylesheet, or template <style> element that holds CSS names it anywhere, as in .name, .card .name, .name:hover, or :is(.name), including inside @media and nested rules, or when an attribute selector such as [class~="name"] or [class^="btn-"] matches it. Citry does not read stylesheets linked by URL, local files that cannot be read as UTF-8, sources written in another language through css_lang, or <link> tags in templates, so their classes are reported. Bound classes, words inside {{ }} in a class attribute, and classes on tags that render no element are not checked, and a class that citry.css.misspelled-class reports is not reported again. citry check needs your application for this rule; the editor does not run it.
diagnostics.fix: Add CSS for the class to a component, or remove the class. For a component that uses classes from a stylesheet Citry does not read, set rule_undeclared_css_class to "ignore" in its Lint class.

messages.default: No CSS that Citry reads styles the class '{name}'.

diagnostics.title: Custom property that nothing sets
diagnostics.summary: A component's CSS reads a custom property with var(--name) and no fallback, and nothing that Citry reads sets it. Unless a stylesheet or script outside Citry sets it, the CSS property that reads it gets its inherited or initial value.
diagnostics.when: The rule is off by default, because it also reports properties that a site stylesheet, a design system, or a script outside Citry sets. With rule_undeclared_css_variable set to "warning" or "error", it reports each var(--name) without a fallback value in a component's own css or css_file when nothing that Citry reads sets --name. Citry counts as setting it: a --name: declaration or an @property --name rule in a registered component's css, css_file, inline or local-file Dependencies stylesheet, or template <style> element that holds CSS; a css_data() or CssData key called name on any registered component; a style attribute in a template that sets --name; and the text --name in quotes, or followed by a colon, in a :style or c-style binding, in a component's JavaScript, or in the Python module that defines a component. A component whose own css_data() keys Citry cannot all read is not checked, but a property that only such a component sets is still reported where another component reads it. A var() in a template's style attribute is not checked, and a var() that citry.css.misspelled-variable reports is not reported again. citry check needs your application for this rule; the editor does not run it.
diagnostics.fix: Set the property in a component's CSS or css_data(), add a fallback, as in var(--name, 1rem), or, for a component that reads properties a stylesheet outside Citry sets, set rule_undeclared_css_variable to "ignore" in its Lint class.

parameters.name: The custom property as written, without the leading --.

messages.default: Nothing that Citry reads sets --{name}, so this property gets its initial or inherited value unless a stylesheet or script outside Citry sets it.

diagnostics.title: Unknown Vue variable
diagnostics.summary: A Vue expression reads a name the component does not send to the browser, often because of a typo. Vue shows nothing, or the expression fails in the browser.
diagnostics.when: A name in a Vue expression is not a JsData or js_data() key, a v-for or slot alias around it, a Vue or Citry helper, a browser global, or a declared vue_variables entry.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or send the value from js_data(). If it is a Python variable, pass it with a c- attribute instead. Declare names that come from outside Citry in vue_variables, or change rule_unknown_vue_variable.

messages.default: Vue variable '{name}' is not available in this component.
messages.python: Vue variable '{name}' is not available in this component. '{name}' is a Python variable here, which the browser never sees; pass its value with a c- attribute or loop with Vue's v-for.

examples.title: Unknown name in a Vue expression

diagnostics.title: Python variable read by a Vue expression
diagnostics.summary: A Vue expression reads a Python c-for or c-fill variable. The browser never sees that variable, so the value is missing, or Vue shows a different browser value with the same name.
diagnostics.when: A Vue expression inside a c-for loop or c-fill binding reads the Python variable, and no Vue v-for or slot alias of that name is around it. When Citry knows every name the component sends to the browser and the name is not among them, it reports citry.vue.unknown-variable instead, unless that rule is set to ignore.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the Python value with a c- attribute, such as c-title="item" instead of :title="item", or loop with Vue's v-for. If a browser value has the same name, rename one of them.

parameters.name: Python variable name read by the Vue expression.
parameters.attribute: HTML attribute name that a c- attribute can set from Python.

messages.default: Vue reads '{name}' from browser state, but '{name}' is a Python variable here. Pass its value with a c- attribute or loop with Vue's v-for instead.
messages.attribute: Vue reads '{name}' from browser state, but '{name}' is a Python variable here. Use c-{attribute}="{name}" to pass the Python value.
messages.browser: Vue reads the component's browser value '{name}' here, not the Python loop or slot variable '{name}'. Pass the Python value with a c- attribute, or rename one of them.
messages.browser-attribute: Vue reads the component's browser value '{name}' here, not the Python loop or slot variable '{name}'. Use c-{attribute}="{name}" for the Python value, or rename one of them.

examples.title: Python loop variable in a Vue binding

diagnostics.title: Vue expression with a syntax error
diagnostics.summary: A Vue expression, such as the value of v-if, :title, or @click, is not valid JavaScript. Vue cannot compile the template, so the page fails when it renders.
diagnostics.when: The expression does not parse as JavaScript, after character references such as && are decoded the way Vue decodes them. Citry names the parser's error in the message and underlines the place it points to, such as the end of open &&. For an expression that holds a character reference, it underlines the whole expression and leaves the parser's error out of the message. A listener may also hold statements or a function expression. The arguments of a server call such as @c-click="save({...})" are checked too. A valueless :title, which Vue reads as :title="title", everything on or inside an element with v-pre, which Vue does not compile, and custom directive values are not checked, although Vue still fails on a custom directive value that is not valid JavaScript. citry check --static and an editor that has not loaded your application report it too, with the severity the component's own Lint class sets as a plain string.
diagnostics.fix: Complete or correct the expression, such as v-if="open && ready".

parameters.attribute: Attribute that holds the expression, as written in the template.
parameters.detail: The JavaScript parser's message, such as Unexpected token.

messages.default: The Vue expression in '{attribute}' is not valid JavaScript, so Vue cannot compile this template.
messages.parser: The Vue expression in '{attribute}' is not valid JavaScript ({detail}), so Vue cannot compile this template.

diagnostics.title: Template that Vue's compiler rejects
diagnostics.summary: Vue's compiler rejects the template, so a component that uses Vue fails to render. Most often the browser would build a different element tree from the one the template describes: a <div> directly inside a <table>, a <button> inside a <button>, a <form> inside a <form>, or an <a> inside an <a>. A v-else with no v-if right before it, and a component inside a Vue v-for, are reported too.
diagnostics.when:
Citry writes the Vue template that a render compiles, runs the same compiler on it, and reports each error at the text you wrote. Every c-if, c-elif and c-else branch, and the body of every c-for, is checked, but usually on its own, so a mistake that spans the c-if or c-for tag, such as a
in a c-for directly inside a , may not be reported. A Vue expression with a syntax error is reported as citry.vue.invalid-expression, and a block element inside a

as citry.template.invalid-nesting, so this rule does not report them again, even when those rules are turned off. A component inside a Vue v-for is reported only by citry check with the application loaded, which can tell whether the component is transparent or simple; such a component renders into its caller's HTML and may sit inside a v-for. Content inside #c-ignore or , whether a 's content fits the tag Python chooses, where a component tag sits, and attributes an extension handles, such as @c-click, are not checked, and a template that uses an extension's own template syntax is skipped. citry check --static and an editor that has not loaded your application report it too, with the severity the component's own Lint class sets as a plain string.
diagnostics.fix: Follow the compiler's message. For a table, put rows in <tr> and cells in <td> or <th>; for nested buttons, forms or links, close the outer one first or use another element; for v-else, put it on the element right after the one with v-if or v-else-if.

parameters.detail: What the compiler found, as one sentence.

messages.default: Vue cannot compile this template: {detail}

examples.title: A div directly inside a table

diagnostics.title: Misspelled DOM event
diagnostics.summary: A listener on an HTML element names an event that looks like a typo of a DOM event, such as @clik for @click. No element fires that event, so the listener never runs.
diagnostics.when: The event name in @name or v-on:name, before any modifier, is all lowercase letters, is not a DOM event that the HTML Standard or Vue's types list, and is one typing slip from one that is: two neighboring letters swapped, one letter typed twice, or one letter left out. Names with a hyphen, a colon, or an uppercase letter, and a few ordinary words such as scrolled and touched, are not reported, because they are usually custom events. Component tags, custom elements, and v-pre content are not checked. citry check --static and an editor that has not loaded your application report it too, with the severity the component's own Lint class sets as a plain string.
diagnostics.fix: Use the event the message names. If the page dispatches a custom event with this name, set rule_misspelled_event to "ignore" for that component.

parameters.event: Event name as written in the template.
parameters.suggestion: The DOM event the author probably meant.

messages.default: '{event}' is not a DOM event, so this listener never runs. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?

diagnostics.title: Unknown component JavaScript variable
diagnostics.summary: Code inside $component reads a name that is not declared there, often a callback value you forgot to destructure. It fails in the browser.
diagnostics.when: A name inside a $component initializer is not declared in that code, destructured from the callback's argument, a JavaScript or browser global, or a declared component_js_globals entry.
diagnostics.fix: Declare or destructure the name, or read the value from the component instance. If a project script defines it as a global, declare it in component_js_globals, or change rule_unknown_component_js_variable.

messages.default: Component JavaScript variable '{name}' is not defined.

diagnostics.title: Unknown component instance member
diagnostics.summary: Component JavaScript reads this.<name> or component.<name>, and the component has no member with that name, often because of a typo. The value is undefined in the browser.
diagnostics.when: The name is not a js_data() key, prop, data() key, setup binding, method, computed value, or injection. Citry checks only when it can see every js_data() key and every Vue Options section in the source. It skips names that start with $ or _, bracket reads such as component[key], and code that uses mixins, extends, Object.assign, a class, or computed member names.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or define it on the component. A plugin that adds a property to every component should give it a $ prefix, such as $api.

messages.default: Component instance member '{name}' is not defined by this component.

examples.title: Misspelled js_data() key in a callback

diagnostics.title: Invalid State binding target
diagnostics.summary: A :c-* State binding is on an element that has no value to bind, such as a <div>, or an input type that cannot hold one, such as a file input.
diagnostics.when: The element or input type cannot hold a bound value, or does not support the binding's direction or update event.
diagnostics.fix: Bind a form control that holds a value, such as <input>, <select>, or <textarea>. On a custom element, name its update event with .on:<event>. To react to an event on another element, use an @c-* binding instead.

parameters.detail: Explanation of the unsupported binding target.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: v-model on an element that holds no value
diagnostics.summary: v-model is on an element that has no value to bind, such as a <form> or a <div>. The component fails to render when Citry compiles it for Vue.
diagnostics.when: v-model, with or without modifiers such as .lazy, is on an HTML element other than <input>, <textarea>, or <select>, or on a custom element such as <my-picker>. Component tags, PascalCase Vue components, and <c-element> are not reported, because they decide what v-model binds; neither is v-pre content, which Vue does not compile. citry check --static and an editor that has not loaded your application report it too, with the severity the component's own Lint class sets as a plain string.
diagnostics.fix: Move v-model to the <input>, <textarea>, or <select> that holds the value. For a custom element, bind its value property and listen for its change event instead.

parameters.tag: Tag name as written in the template.

messages.default: v-model does not work on <{tag}>, which holds no value. Put it on an <input>, <textarea>, or <select>, or on a component.

diagnostics.title: Unknown State binding field
diagnostics.summary: A :c-* State binding names a field the component's State does not have, often because of a typo.
diagnostics.when: A :c-* binding names a field that is not a public field of the component's State class. Bindings whose component or State class Citry cannot determine are not checked.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the field name, or add the field to the component's State class.

parameters.name: Authored State field name, without prefix or modifiers.

messages.default: State field '{name}' is not a public field of this component.

examples.title: Unknown field in a State binding

diagnostics.title: Unknown server event
diagnostics.summary: Browser code names a server event that the component has no handler for, often because of a typo.
diagnostics.when: A template or component JavaScript calls sendEvent, $sendEvent, $loading, or $error with a string that names no handler, or an @c-* binding names no handler.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or add a public method with that name to the component's Events class.

messages.default: Server event '{name}' is not declared by this component.

diagnostics.title: Undeclared emitted event
diagnostics.summary: Browser code emits a Vue event that the component's emits option does not list, often because of a typo. Parents listening for the declared name never hear it.
diagnostics.when: this.$emit, component.$emit, or $emit in the component's template uses a name that emits does not list and no on<Event> prop declares. Citry checks only when emits is an array of strings or an object with plain keys. A component without emits may emit any name, as in Vue.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the event name, or add it to emits.

messages.default: Event '{name}' is not declared in this component's emits option.

diagnostics.title: Listener for an event the child component does not declare
diagnostics.summary: A template listens on a child component for an event the child does not declare, often because of a typo. The listener usually never runs.
diagnostics.when: An @name or v-on:name listener on a component tag names an event that the child's emits does not list and no on<Event> prop accepts. Vue then passes the listener to the child's root element, where it runs only for a DOM event of that name. A plain lowercase name, such as hdie, is reported only when it is not a DOM event that the HTML Standard or Vue's types list, such as click. Citry checks only when the child's emits is an array of strings or an object with plain keys. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the event name, or add it to the child's emits. It is a warning by default; to make an undeclared listener fail citry check, set rule_undeclared_component_event to "error".

parameters.component: Component tag, lowercased, including the c- prefix.
parameters.name: Authored event name.
parameters.suggestion: The declared event closest to the written name.

messages.default: Component '{component}' does not declare event '{name}' in its emits option.
messages.suggestion: Component '{component}' does not declare event '{name}' in its emits option. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?

diagnostics.title: Missing required Vue prop
diagnostics.summary: A component tag leaves out a Vue prop that the child component marks as required.
diagnostics.when: A registered <c-*> tag has no Vue binding for a prop the child declares with required: true, and no spread binding could supply it.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the prop on the tag, such as :count="total".

messages.default: Required Vue prop '{name}' is missing for <{tag}>.

diagnostics.title: Incompatible Vue prop
diagnostics.summary: A Vue prop on a component tag gets a value of a type the child component does not accept.
diagnostics.when: A :prop or v-bind:prop value on a component tag has a type Citry knows, from a literal, a condition whose two results are literals, JsData, or a loop binding, and the child's declared Vue prop type does not accept it. For a Boolean prop, Vue turns the string '' and the prop's own name, hyphenated, into true, so any other string literal is reported.
diagnostics.fix: Pass a value of the type the child declares, or change the child's prop type.

parameters.name: Authored native Vue prop name.
parameters.expected: Child component's accepted Vue prop type.

messages.default: Vue prop '{name}' expects {expected}, but this binding is {actual}.

examples.title: A string for a Boolean prop

diagnostics.title: Repeated component without #c-key
diagnostics.summary: A component that a <c-for> loop repeats has no #c-key, on a page that uses Vue. The page fails to render as soon as the loop has two items.
diagnostics.when: A registered component tag sits inside a <c-for> body, or carries c-for itself, and has no #c-key. It is reported when the template's component or the repeated component makes the page use Vue: it has component JavaScript, js_data() or JsData, an Events class, or a Vue attribute (v-*, @, or :) in its template. A transparent component and a simple=True component are not reported, because they render into their caller's HTML. Another component on the same page can also make it use Vue, which this check cannot see. citry check needs your application for this rule.
diagnostics.fix: Add #c-key with a value that identifies each item and stays the same, such as #c-key="task.id".

parameters.tag: Component tag as written in the template.

messages.default: <{tag}> repeats inside <c-for> but has no #c-key. This page uses Vue, and the render fails when the loop has two items.

diagnostics.title: Assignment to a Vue prop
diagnostics.summary: A component changes a prop it receives from its parent. Vue props are read-only, so the assignment does not change the value and Vue logs a warning instead.
diagnostics.when: In the component's own template, a Vue expression assigns to one of the component's declared props with =, +=, or another assignment operator, or with ++ or --, or binds it with v-model. In the component's JavaScript, it is reported for an assignment or update through this or the $component context, such as this.open = false or this.count++. A write to a field of an object prop, such as open.count = 1, is not reported, and neither is a name that a v-for or slot binds. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Emit an event and let the parent change the value, as in $emit('close'), or copy the prop into the component's own data and change the copy.

messages.default: Prop '{name}' is read-only, so this assignment does not change it. Emit an event to let the parent change it.
messages.v-model: v-model writes to prop '{name}', which is read-only, so the input cannot change it. Emit an event to let the parent change it.

diagnostics.title: Unknown server event field
diagnostics.summary: An @c-* binding sends an object with a key that the handler's data class does not declare. The server rejects the call, and the handler does not run.
diagnostics.when: The arguments of an @c-* binding, such as @c-click="save({amont: 1})", are an object literal with a key the handler's data class does not declare, or the handler takes no data parameter. A key written next to a ... spread is still checked. A Pydantic data class is not checked, because Pydantic may ignore extra keys or read a field under another name. When several components share the template, it is checked only when they use the same data class for the handler. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the key, or add the field to the handler's data class.

parameters.name: The key as written.
parameters.suggestion: The declared field one typing slip from the key.

messages.default: Server event '{event}' has no field '{name}', so the server rejects this call.
messages.suggestion: Server event '{event}' has no field '{name}', so the server rejects this call. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?
messages.no-data: Server event '{event}' takes no data, so the server rejects this call because of field '{name}'.

examples.title: A typo in a field name

diagnostics.title: Unknown form field
diagnostics.summary: A form sends its fields to a server event, and one of its controls has a name that the handler's data class does not declare. The server rejects each submit that sends that control, and the handler does not run.
diagnostics.when: A <form> has an @c-submit binding that writes no arguments, such as @c-submit.prevent="search" or search(), so the browser sends the form's named controls, as a post without JavaScript does. An <input>, <select>, <textarea>, or submit <button> in the form has a static name the handler's data class does not declare, or the handler takes no data parameter. A submit button sends its name only when it is the one that submits the form, and a checkbox only when it is checked. A control is not checked when the browser may not send it with this form or may send it under another name: it is disabled, by its own disabled attribute, a bound :disabled, or a disabled <fieldset>; it is tied to another form by its form attribute; it is a file input, a button that cannot submit, or a button whose click is prevented, as in @click.prevent; its type or name is written as an expression; or it has an attribute spread such as v-bind="attrs". An image input sends where it was clicked, as x and y, or name.x and name.y, so those names are checked instead of its name. Neither are the host's CSRF field names that the server removes before it checks the data class, by default csrfmiddlewaretoken. A Pydantic data class is not checked, because Pydantic converts values and may read a field under another name. When several components share the template, it is checked only when they use the same data class for the handler. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the control's name, or add the field to the handler's data class.

parameters.name: The control's name as written.
parameters.suggestion: The declared field one typing slip from the name.

messages.default: The form sends field '{name}', which server event '{event}' does not declare, so the server rejects the submit.
messages.suggestion: The form sends field '{name}', which server event '{event}' does not declare, so the server rejects the submit. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?
messages.no-data: The form sends field '{name}', but server event '{event}' takes no data, so the server rejects the submit.

examples.title: A typo in a control's name

diagnostics.title: Missing form field
diagnostics.summary: A form sends its fields to a server event, but none of its controls is named after a field that the handler's data class requires. The server rejects every submit, and the handler does not run.
diagnostics.when: A <form> has an @c-submit binding that writes no arguments, such as @c-submit.prevent="search" or search(), so the browser sends the form's named controls, as a post without JavaScript does. No <input>, <select>, <textarea>, or <button> in the form has the name of a field without a default. The rule runs only when the template shows every name the form can send: the form has no id, which a control elsewhere could name in its form attribute, and it holds no component, custom element, slot, <template>, loop, v-html, #c-ignore content, attribute spread, or name written as an expression. A Pydantic data class is not checked, because Pydantic converts values and may read a field under another name. When several components share the template, it is checked only when they use the same data class for the handler. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Add a control with that name, or give the field a default in the handler's data class.

messages.default: Server event '{event}' requires field '{name}', but no control in this form has that name, so the server rejects every submit.

examples.title: A form without the required control

diagnostics.title: Missing server event field
diagnostics.summary: An @c-* binding calls a server event without a field that the handler's data class requires. The server rejects the call, and the handler does not run.
diagnostics.when: The arguments of an @c-* binding are an object literal with no ... spread and no computed key, and they leave out a field that has no default; or the binding sends no arguments, as in save or save(), from an element that cannot contain a form, such as a button. A binding with no arguments on a <form>, or for the submit event, is not reported here, because the browser then sends the form's fields; citry.browser.missing-form-field checks those. A Pydantic data class is not checked. When several components share the template, it is checked only when they use the same data class for the handler. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Send the field, or give it a default in the handler's data class.

messages.default: Server event '{event}' requires field '{name}', which this call does not send, so the server rejects it.

examples.title: No arguments for a required field

diagnostics.title: Wrong type for a server event field
diagnostics.summary: An @c-* binding sends a literal value that the handler's data class does not accept for that field. The server rejects the call, and the handler does not run.
diagnostics.when: A key in the object literal of an @c-* binding has a literal value, such as '1', true, 2.5, or null, or a condition whose two results are literals, and the server's check for that field rejects it. The browser sends the arguments as JSON, which the server checks strictly: a string is not turned into a number. For a handler that accepts GET, the browser may send them as a query string instead, which the server reads as text, so a value is reported only when both ways fail. Values that are not literals are not checked. A Pydantic data class is not checked, because Pydantic converts values. When several components share the template, it is checked only when they use the same data class for the handler. citry check needs your application for this rule, and the editor reports it once it has loaded your application.
diagnostics.fix: Send a value of the type the field declares, such as 1 instead of '1'.

parameters.name: The field's name.
parameters.detail: The server's message for this value.

messages.default: Server event '{event}' rejects this value for field '{name}': {detail}

examples.title: A string for an int field

diagnostics.title: Template declaration unavailable
diagnostics.summary: citry check could not read a component's template or template_file, for example because computing it raised an error.
diagnostics.when: Reading the component's template or template_file declaration raises an error, or Citry cannot tell which declaration applies.
diagnostics.fix: Read the error in the message and fix the declaration or the code it runs.

messages.default: Citry could not inspect this component's template declaration: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Unsupported template language
diagnostics.summary: The component sets template_lang to another template language. citry check reads only Citry templates, so it skipped this one.
diagnostics.when: A component's template_lang is not None.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix if the other language is intended. Check that template with that language's own tools.

parameters.type: Runtime type of the non-None template_lang value.

messages.default: Citry cannot check template_lang with a {type} value. This template was skipped.

diagnostics.title: Invalid template declaration value
diagnostics.summary: A component's template or template_file has a value of the wrong type, so citry check skipped it.
diagnostics.when: Component.template is not a string, or Component.template_file is neither a string nor a pathlib.Path.
diagnostics.fix: Set template to a string, or template_file to a string or Path.

messages.inline: Component.template must be a string. This template was skipped.
messages.file: Component.template_file must be a string or Path. This template was skipped.

diagnostics.title: Template file not found
diagnostics.summary: The file named in template_file does not exist in any place Citry looks.
diagnostics.when: template_file points to a path that is not in the component's directory or any configured template directory.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the path, or move the file to one of the searched locations the message lists.

messages.default: Template file '{path}' was not found. Searched: {locations}.

diagnostics.title: Template file could not be read
diagnostics.summary: The template file exists, but Citry could not open it or read it as UTF-8 text.
diagnostics.when: Citry finds the template_file but cannot open it, or it is not valid UTF-8.
diagnostics.fix: Check the file's permissions, and save it as UTF-8.

messages.default: Citry could not read this template file: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Template variables unavailable
diagnostics.summary: citry check could not work out which variables a component's template receives, so it cannot check them.
diagnostics.when: Reading the component's declared or inferred template data raises an error.
diagnostics.fix: Read the error in the message and fix the template data declaration or the code it runs.

messages.default: Citry could not inspect this template's variables: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Template checked only with the application
diagnostics.summary: A class sets a template, but it extends a class from another module of your project, so Citry cannot tell from the file alone that it is a component. Its template is checked only when Citry loads your application and finds the class there.
diagnostics.when: A class in a Python file sets template to a string literal that contains a tag, Citry cannot prove from that file that the class is a component, and it extends a class imported from a module of your project, directly or through a class defined in the same file. A class from an installed package does not count. citry check --static lists it as a note. The editor shows it as information on the class name while it has not loaded your application, and for a class added or renamed since it loaded the application. citry check with your application loaded, citry check --types, and an editor that has loaded the application find the class in the component registry and check its template, so they do not report it.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing is wrong with the code. To check the template, load your application: run citry check with it, as in citry --app module:engine check, and give the editor the same module:engine path, in the citry.app setting in VS Code. For a class you added or renamed, the message stays until the editor loads the application again, which VS Code does when you save a Python file.

parameters.base: The imported class it extends, as written.

messages.default: Citry cannot tell from this file that {component} is a component, because it extends {base}, which comes from another module, so this template is checked only when Citry loads your application and finds {component} there.

examples.title: A base class from another module
examples.source:
from app.base import BaseCard


class Card(BaseCard):
    template = """
      <article>{{ title }}</article>
    """

diagnostics.title: Links not checked
diagnostics.summary: citry check did not check the link paths in your templates, because no web framework integration told Citry which paths your app serves.
diagnostics.when: A template has an href, src, or action path that starts with a single /, rule_unknown_url is not "ignore" for it, and no citry.contrib.flask.mount(), citry.contrib.fastapi.mount(), or citry.contrib.django.urlpatterns() call ran while citry check loaded your application. This happens when the module the --app option names only creates the Citry instance and nothing imports the module that mounts it, or when you serve Citry with citry.contrib.asgi or citry.contrib.wsgi, which do not know your app's routes. citry check lists it once, as a note, and it never fails the check.
diagnostics.fix: Point --app at a module that mounts Citry when it is imported, such as app.main:citry_app when app/main.py calls mount(app, citry_app), or config.urls:citry_app, with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE set, for a Django project whose urls.py calls urlpatterns(). To stop checking links, set rule_unknown_url to "ignore".

parameters.path: One of the paths that were not checked.

messages.default: Links such as '{path}' were not checked, because no web framework integration told Citry which paths your app serves. Point --app at the module that calls citry.contrib.flask.mount(), citry.contrib.fastapi.mount(), or citry.contrib.django.urlpatterns(), or set rule_unknown_url to "ignore".

diagnostics.title: Link check failed
diagnostics.summary: Your web framework raised an error while citry check asked whether your app serves a link path, so citry check skipped that link.
diagnostics.when: The path checker that citry.contrib.flask.mount(), citry.contrib.fastapi.mount(), or citry.contrib.django.urlpatterns() registered raises an error for one or more link paths. Each of those paths is skipped, and citry check lists one note with the error for the skipped path that sorts first. The note never fails the check.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the error the message shows. It comes from your framework's routing code, such as a URL pattern module that fails to import. Until it is fixed, citry check skips those links.

parameters.path: The skipped path that sorts first.

messages.default: Citry skipped the link path '{path}', because asking your web framework whether your app serves it raised an error: {detail}
messages.several: Citry skipped {count} link paths, such as '{path}', because asking your web framework whether your app serves them raised an error: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Python source could not be analyzed
diagnostics.summary: A Python file could not be read or parsed, so its components were not checked.
diagnostics.when: citry check --static reaches a Python file it cannot read, decode, or parse.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the Python syntax error or encoding problem in the file the message names.

messages.default: Citry could not analyze this Python source: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Invalid Fluent catalog source
diagnostics.summary: A messages block or Fluent catalog file has invalid Fluent syntax or another translation source mistake.
diagnostics.when: A messages block or catalog file has invalid Fluent syntax, an unsupported @param type, or another source error.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the Fluent source at the reported position. The message says what is wrong.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Unknown i18n message
diagnostics.summary: Code asks for a translation message that no catalog defines, often because of a typo in the message ID.
diagnostics.when: A tr() call, <c-trans> tag, $c-tr binding, or browser bind() call with a literal ID names a message or attribute that no component or configured catalog package defines.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the message ID, or add the message to the component's messages or a catalog.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Invalid i18n argument
diagnostics.summary: A translation call passes the wrong inputs: a missing, extra, or mistyped argument, an unknown format profile, or wrong <c-trans> values or fills.
diagnostics.when: A literal i18n call or $c-tr binding is malformed, its message inputs do not match the message's @param declarations, it names an unknown formatter or parser profile, or a <c-trans> tag supplies the wrong values or fills.
diagnostics.fix: Match the arguments to the message's @param declarations, which hover shows, or correct the profile name.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Message variable without a type
diagnostics.summary: A message uses a variable that has no # @param comment, so Citry cannot check the type of the value that callers pass in.
diagnostics.when: A source-language message uses a variable such as { $name } in its value or an attribute, has no # @param comment declaring its type, and rule_i18n_missing_param_type is "warning". A variable used in a selector or a formatting function without a type fails catalog compilation and is reported as citry.i18n.catalog-invalid.
diagnostics.fix: Add a comment such as # @param {str} $name above the message, naming the type the variable really takes. Set rule_i18n_missing_param_type to "error" to make a missing type fail catalog compilation, or to "ignore" to hide this warning.

parameters.detail: Message and variable that lack a type.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Text from a fallback language
diagnostics.summary: A translation is missing for some locales, so this text appears in another language there. The page still renders, but the text sits inside an element marked with the requested language, so a screen reader may read it with the wrong pronunciation.
diagnostics.when: A tr() call or self.i18n.tr() call with a literal message ID, or a message listed in Component.I18n.client_messages, has no translation in some selectable locale and resolves to another locale through the configured fallbacks or the message's source locale.
diagnostics.fix: Add the missing translations; the i18n coverage command lists them. To show fallback text with its own language, call self.i18n.resolve() and put its locale and direction on an element, as the i18n guide's Language direction and accessibility page shows. Set rule_i18n_cross_language_fallback to "error" to require complete translations, or to "ignore" to hide this warning.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Rich message without a translation
diagnostics.summary: A <c-trans> message has no translation in some locale. Rendering it in that locale raises I18nRuntimeUnavailableError, because <c-trans> adds no element that could mark text from a fallback language.
diagnostics.when: A <c-trans> tag names a message or attribute that has no translation in some selectable locale, so it would resolve to another locale through the configured fallbacks or the message's source locale.
diagnostics.fix: Add a translation for each locale the finding lists. Plain text messages may fall back; only <c-trans> needs every translation.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Unknown client i18n message
diagnostics.summary: Component.I18n.client_messages names a message that does not exist, so the browser cannot load it.
diagnostics.when: Component.I18n.client_messages names a message ID that no component or configured catalog package defines.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name in client_messages, or add the message.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Invalid template syntax
diagnostics.summary: The template has a syntax error, so the formatter left it unchanged.
diagnostics.when: A format command receives a template with a Citry syntax error.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the syntax error, then format again.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Invalid formatter directive
diagnostics.summary: A fmt: on, fmt: off, or fmt: skip comment has no matching partner or sits where it cannot apply.
diagnostics.when: A formatter directive has no valid scope at the place it is written, such as a fmt: on without an earlier fmt: off.
diagnostics.fix: Pair each fmt: off with a fmt: on in the same scope, or remove the stray directive.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Formatter safety check failed
diagnostics.summary: The formatter's own safety check failed, so it refused to change the file. Your template is not at fault.
diagnostics.when: The formatted result fails one of Citry's safety checks, for example formatting it a second time would change it again.
diagnostics.fix: The file is unchanged. Report the template and message as a Citry bug.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Formatting shape unsupported
diagnostics.summary: The template is valid, but the formatter cannot rewrite this shape safely, so it left it unchanged.
diagnostics.when: The template's structure is outside what the formatter can rewrite.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Format that part by hand, or wrap it in fmt: off and fmt: on.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Embedded formatter returned invalid output
diagnostics.summary: The JavaScript or CSS formatter returned a change that does not fit the code it was asked to format, so Citry discarded it.
diagnostics.when: An external JavaScript or CSS formatter returns an edit outside the region Citry sent it.
diagnostics.fix: The file is unchanged. Try another formatter for that language, or report the message.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Embedded formatting suppressed
diagnostics.summary: A fmt: off or fmt: skip comment kept a JavaScript or CSS region unformatted, as requested.
diagnostics.when: A fmt: off or fmt: skip directive covers an embedded JavaScript or CSS region.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Remove the directive if you want the region formatted.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Embedded language unsupported
diagnostics.summary: A <script> or <style> region declares a language Citry has no formatter for, so it was left unchanged.
diagnostics.when: An embedded script or style region declares a language that no Citry formatter handles.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Format that region with its own tools.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Embedded interpolation unsupported
diagnostics.summary: A JavaScript or CSS region contains Citry interpolation, such as {{ title }}, so it was left unchanged.
diagnostics.when: An embedded JavaScript or CSS region contains Citry interpolation, which an external formatter cannot handle safely.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the value through js_data() or css_data() instead of interpolating it, or leave the region unformatted.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Embedded formatter unavailable
diagnostics.summary: No JavaScript or CSS formatter answered, so that region was left unchanged.
diagnostics.when: Citry asks the editor to format embedded JavaScript or CSS, and no installed formatter returns an edit.
diagnostics.fix: In VS Code, check that Prettier for VS Code is installed and enabled for the language, or disable it so Citry uses its own copy of Prettier.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Invalid Python host syntax
diagnostics.summary: The Python file has a syntax error, so Citry could not find the component strings to format.
diagnostics.when: A format command targets a Python file that is not valid Python.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the Python syntax error, then format again.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Document is not eligible for formatting
diagnostics.summary: The file or cursor position is not inside a Citry template, script, or style, so there is nothing to format.
diagnostics.when: Citry cannot tell that the document or cursor position belongs to a template, js, or css string, or a standalone Citry template.
diagnostics.fix: Place the cursor inside a template, js, or css string, or open the template file itself.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Document changed during formatting
diagnostics.summary: The document changed while Citry was formatting it, so the result was discarded.
diagnostics.when: The document changes after Citry prepares the edit and before the editor applies it.
diagnostics.fix: Run the format command again.

messages.default: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Formatting cancelled
diagnostics.summary: Formatting was cancelled before Citry applied it.
diagnostics.when: The editor or you cancel a format request before Citry applies its edits.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Run the format command again if needed.
